items.title: A Gate Change
items.text: When Hana reached the check-in counter, the agent told her that her flight had been moved from gate 12 to gate 31 because of a mechanical check. Hana had already walked for twenty minutes with her heavy bag, so she felt a little annoyed, but she kept her voice calm. "I understand this isn't your decision," she said, "but could you tell me whether I will still make my connecting flight?" The agent typed for a moment and explained that the connecting plane waits for delayed passengers, so there was no real danger. She then handed Hana a voucher for a free snack and a map with the new route marked in yellow. Hana thanked her, smiled, and decided that a polite question had worked better than a complaint would have.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How an airline punished a passenger who arrived late at the counter
How a calm, polite attitude helped a traveler deal with an unexpected change
Why mechanical checks make most flights leave earlier than planned
How a traveler chose between two different gates for her flight
qs.why: 공항에서 게이트가 바뀐 상황에서 하나가 침착하고 공손하게 질문해 도움을 받은 이야기예요.

qs.q: Why was the gate changed?
o: The plane needed a mechanical check.
The first gate was closed for the night.
Too many passengers wanted to board early.
The connecting plane had left without Hana.
qs.why: 첫 문장에서 mechanical check 때문에 게이트가 바뀌었다고 해요.

qs.q: Why did Hana say, "I understand this isn't your decision"?
o: She wanted to prove to the agent and to other passengers that a serious mistake had been made.
She hoped to be given a seat in a higher travel class.
She was trying to end the conversation as quickly as possible.
She wanted to show she did not blame the agent while still asking for help.
qs.why: 상대를 탓하지 않는다는 점을 먼저 밝혀 공손하게 도움을 청한 표현이에요.

qs.q: The word "annoyed" is closest in meaning to
o: amazed
relieved
irritated
confused
qs.why: annoyed는 '짜증이 난'이라는 뜻으로 irritated와 가장 가까워요.

qs.q: What did the agent give Hana?
o: A new ticket and a refund for the first flight
A food voucher and a map showing the new route
A bus pass and a list of nearby hotels
A phone card and a printed weather report
qs.why: agent가 snack voucher와 새 경로가 표시된 지도를 줬다고 해요.

items.title: Email to a Restaurant Manager
items.text:
Dear Mr. Alvarez,

I visited your restaurant last Friday with my family to celebrate my grandmother's birthday. We enjoyed the food very much, and the soup was the best I have ever tasted. However, we waited almost fifty minutes for our main dishes, and nobody explained the delay. When I asked a waiter about it, he only said, "It's busy tonight." I understand that Friday evenings can be hectic, but a short apology or an estimate of the waiting time would have made a big difference. I am writing not to ask for a refund but to share my honest impression, because I would like to come back. I hope this feedback is useful to you and your team.

Sincerely,
Minjun Oh

qs.q: Why did Minjun write this email?
o: To give honest feedback so that the service could improve
To demand his money back for the whole meal and a written apology
To book a table for another family event
To ask for the recipe of the soup he liked
qs.why: 마지막 부분에서 환불을 요구하려는 것이 아니라 솔직한 인상을 전하려는 것이라고 밝혀요.

qs.q: What did Minjun think would have helped most?
o: A free dessert for each member of the family
A larger menu with more choices for the main dishes
A table closer to the kitchen so food arrived faster
A brief apology or an estimate of the waiting time
qs.why: short apology or an estimate of the waiting time이 큰 차이를 만들었을 거라고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Minjun's overall opinion of the restaurant?
o: He believes the food was disappointing and overpriced.
He thinks the waiter was rude on purpose.
He liked the food and still wants to return.
He plans to write a review that discourages customers.
qs.why: 음식을 매우 즐겼고 다시 오고 싶다고 하므로 전반적으로 긍정적이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "hectic" is closest in meaning to
o: quiet and peaceful
very busy and full of activity
expensive and fancy enough for special celebrations
cold and uncomfortable
qs.why: hectic은 '정신없이 바쁜'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What was the waiter's reply when Minjun asked about the delay?
o: He briefly said the restaurant was busy.
He promised to bring the dishes in five minutes.
He offered a discount on the next visit.
He sent the manager to the family's table.
qs.why: waiter는 'It's busy tonight.'라고만 말했어요.

items.title: A Voicemail from the Dental Office
items.text: "Hello, this is Clara from Bright Smile Dental. I am calling for Daniel Park. Unfortunately, Dr. Reyes has been called away for a family matter, so we need to move your appointment from Tuesday at three o'clock. We are very sorry for the inconvenience. We have two openings: Wednesday at ten in the morning, or Thursday at four in the afternoon. Both would take about forty minutes. If neither works for you, we can also look at next week. Please call us back at the front desk before five o'clock today, and have your insurance card ready, because we will need to check your information again. If we do not hear from you, we will keep your name on the waiting list. Thank you, and have a lovely day."

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the message?
o: To remind the patient to bring a payment for his visit
To announce that the office is closing permanently
To explain how the patient should clean his teeth
To ask the patient to choose a new time for his appointment
qs.why: Dr. Reyes가 자리를 비워 예약을 옮겨야 하므로 새 시간을 고르라는 전화예요.

qs.q: Why does the office need to change the appointment?
o: The patient asked to come on a different day because of his work.
The office is being repainted this week.
The dentist cannot be there because of a family matter.
The insurance company refused the earlier booking.
qs.why: family matter 때문에 Dr. Reyes가 자리를 비운다고 해요.

qs.q: What should Daniel do before five o'clock today?
o: Visit the office to pick up his new card
Call the front desk and keep his insurance card nearby
Send an email with a list of his free days
Wait for another call on Wednesday morning
qs.why: front desk에 전화하고 보험 카드를 준비하라고 해요.

qs.q: What will happen if Daniel does not respond?
o: His name will stay on a waiting list.
His appointment will be cancelled without notice.
He will be charged an extra fee for the delay.
Dr. Reyes will visit him at home.
qs.why: 연락이 없으면 대기자 명단에 이름을 남겨 둔다고 해요.

items.title: A Quieter Room, Please
items.text: Late one evening, Jiwoo came down to the hotel lobby in her slippers. Her room faced the street, and a group of people were laughing loudly outside. At the desk, a young clerk greeted her with a tired smile. "I'm sorry to bother you," Jiwoo began, "but would it be possible to move to a room at the back? I have an important exam tomorrow morning, and I'm afraid I can't sleep with this noise." The clerk checked his screen and said that only one quiet room was free, on a higher floor, and it was slightly smaller. Jiwoo said she didn't mind. He called a porter to carry her bag, apologized once more, and gave her a coupon for breakfast. Within ten minutes, she was in her new room, and the street sounds had disappeared.

qs.q: What did Jiwoo want from the clerk?
o: A larger room with a view of the city
A later checkout time on the next day
A wake-up call before her exam
A room away from the street noise
qs.why: 소음 때문에 뒤쪽의 조용한 방으로 옮기고 싶다고 했어요.

qs.q: How did Jiwoo begin her request?
o: By telling him sharply that the hotel had made a very serious mistake with her booking
By threatening to leave a bad review on the Internet
By apologizing for troubling him and asking if a change was possible
By asking him to speak to the people outside
qs.why: 'I'm sorry to bother you ... would it be possible'로 정중하게 시작했어요.

qs.q: What is true about the new room?
o: It was on a lower floor, next to the lobby, and just as large as before.
It was quiet but a little smaller than the first one.
It was bigger and had a free breakfast included.
It was the same size and faced the street.
qs.why: 조용한 방이 한 개 남았고 조금 더 작다고 했어요.

qs.q: The phrase "she didn't mind" means that Jiwoo
o: was willing to accept the smaller room
did not understand the clerk's offer
could not remember which room she had
had already decided to leave the hotel
qs.why: didn't mind는 '개의치 않는다, 괜찮다'는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why did the clerk give Jiwoo a coupon?
o: To thank her for staying many nights
To celebrate that she passed an exam
To persuade her to book the hotel again next year
To make up for the trouble she had experienced
qs.why: 그가 거듭 사과하면서 불편에 대한 보상으로 쿠폰을 준 거예요.

items.title: At the Pharmacy Counter
items.text: A pharmacist at a neighborhood shop often explains the same things to different customers. Yesterday she told a student, "Take one tablet with a full glass of water after breakfast and one after dinner. Do not take them on an empty stomach, because it may upset your stomach. If you feel dizzy, stop and call the doctor who wrote your prescription." The student repeated the instructions in his own words to be sure he had understood, and the pharmacist nodded and wrote the times on the box with a marker. "Most people forget to check the expiry date," she added, "so please look at it before you buy any medicine." He thanked her, put the box in his bag, and set two alarms on his phone to remind himself.

qs.q: According to the pharmacist, when should the student take the tablets?
o: Before bed and again at noon
Only when he feels pain
After breakfast and after dinner
Before breakfast on an empty stomach
qs.why: 아침 식사 후와 저녁 식사 후에 하나씩 먹으라고 해요.

qs.q: Why did the student repeat the instructions?
o: To practice speaking English with the pharmacist
To make sure that he had understood them correctly
To show that he had already taken the medicine
To ask for a lower price for the box
qs.why: 자기 말로 되풀이해 이해했는지 확인하려는 거예요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the sentence beginning "Most people forget"?
o: To give an additional piece of useful advice
To criticize the student for his mistake with the earlier prescription
To explain why the shop has few customers
To change the subject to the weather
qs.why: 유통기한을 확인하라는 추가 조언이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the student?
o: He has no interest in what the pharmacist says.
He plans to stop the medicine after a day.
He is afraid of speaking with doctors.
He is careful and wants to follow the directions correctly.
qs.why: 알람을 두 개 설정한 것으로 보아 지시를 잘 따르려는 신중한 사람이에요.

items.title: Hello, Everyone!
items.text: Good afternoon, everyone. My name is Sora Han, and I'm a second-year student in Class 4. Some of you may know me as the girl who plays the cello in the school orchestra. I started learning it at the age of nine, when my grandfather gave me his old instrument. At first I practiced only because he asked me to, but now I practice because I really love the deep sound of it. Outside of music, I enjoy baking bread with my brother and taking photographs of old buildings in my neighborhood. I'm joining the Photography Club this year because I want to learn how to tell stories through pictures. I'm a little nervous, but I'm also excited to meet all of you and learn from you. Thank you for listening.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this speech?
o: To invite classmates to a music concert
To explain how to bake bread at home
To introduce herself to new club members
To argue that photography is better than music
qs.why: 새 부원들에게 자신을 소개하는 연설이에요.

qs.q: Why did Sora first start playing the cello?
o: She wanted to join the orchestra at school and perform at the festival.
Her grandfather asked her to practice with his old instrument.
Her brother challenged her to a contest.
A music teacher said she had natural talent.
qs.why: 처음엔 할아버지가 부탁해서 연습했다고 해요.

qs.q: What does Sora feel about the cello now?
o: She enjoys its deep sound and practices willingly.
She wants to stop because it is too heavy to carry to school.
She feels bored but continues out of duty.
She thinks the old instrument is worth money.
qs.why: 소리를 정말 좋아해서 이제는 스스로 연습한다고 해요.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as one of Sora's interests?
o: Baking bread
Photographing old buildings
Playing the cello
Hiking in the mountains
qs.why: 산행은 언급되지 않았어요. 나머지는 모두 본문에 나와요.

qs.q: How does Sora feel at the end of her speech?
o: Completely calm and bored
Angry about the club's rules
A bit nervous but also excited
Sad about leaving the orchestra
qs.why: I'm a little nervous, but I'm also excited라고 말해요.

items.title: A Photograph of the Market
items.text: The photograph shows a crowded outdoor market on a sunny morning. In the foreground, an elderly woman in a green apron is arranging pyramids of oranges on a wooden table. Beside her, a boy of about ten is holding a paper bag and looking up at the fruit with curiosity. Behind them, colorful umbrellas protect the stalls from the sun, and the people under them seem to be bargaining over the price of vegetables. On the right side of the picture, a street musician is playing a violin, though hardly anyone is paying attention to him. What I like most about this image is the way light falls on the oranges, which makes them look almost like small suns. It gives me the feeling of a warm, lively day.

qs.q: Where is the elderly woman in the photograph?
o: Behind the umbrellas, bargaining over vegetables
In the foreground, arranging oranges
On the right side, playing the violin
Beside the boy, carrying a paper bag
qs.why: 할머니는 앞쪽에서 오렌지를 쌓고 있어요.

qs.q: What is the boy doing?
o: Looking at the fruit while holding a bag
Helping to carry boxes to the stalls
Paying the woman for the oranges
Listening to the musician play
qs.why: 종이봉투를 들고 과일을 호기심 있게 올려다봐요.

qs.q: What does the speaker imply about the street musician?
o: He is the main attraction of the market.
He plays more loudly than the sellers talk.
He is teaching the boy to play.
Few people are listening to him.
qs.why: though hardly anyone is paying attention to him이라고 해요.

qs.q: The phrase "small suns" is used to describe
o: the heat that came from the busy market stalls at noon
the round shape of the umbrellas
the bright look of the oranges in the light
the faces of the happy shoppers
qs.why: 빛을 받은 오렌지가 작은 태양처럼 보인다는 비유예요.

qs.q: What is the overall mood the speaker describes?
o: Dark and lonely
Warm and lively
Quiet and serious
Tense and hurried
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 따뜻하고 활기찬 하루의 느낌이라고 해요.

items.title: Borrowing an E-Book
items.text: Borrowing an e-book from our school library is easy, and you can do it from your phone. First, log in to the library website with your student number and the password you use in class. Second, type the title or the author's name in the search box and press Enter. Third, if the book has a green "Available" label, select it and tap the Borrow button. If the label is red, you can press Reserve, and you will receive an email when it is ready. After that, open the app and download the file; you can read it without an Internet connection. Please note that each book is borrowed for fourteen days. When the time is up, the file closes by itself, so there is no need to return it. If you need more time, you can renew it once, unless another student is waiting.

qs.q: What should a student do first?
o: Log in with a student number and password
Search for a book by its title or author
Press the Reserve button on the book page
Download the library app to the phone
qs.why: 첫 단계는 학번과 비밀번호로 로그인하는 거예요.

qs.q: What does a red label mean in the passage?
o: The book has been permanently removed.
The book can be read only on the computers inside the school library.
The student has already borrowed too many books.
The book is not available now, but it can be reserved.
qs.why: 빨간 표시일 때는 Reserve를 눌러 예약하라고 해요.

qs.q: What happens after fourteen days?
o: The student must pay a late fee.
The student must return the book to the desk.
The file closes automatically.
The app deletes the student's account.
qs.why: 기간이 끝나면 파일이 저절로 닫혀서 반납할 필요가 없어요.

qs.q: When can a student NOT renew an e-book?
o: When the book has a green label
When another student is waiting for it
When he or she has no Internet connection
When fourteen days have not yet passed
qs.why: 다른 학생이 기다리고 있지 않은 한 한 번 연장할 수 있다고 해요.

items.title: A Plan That Needs Fixing
items.text: On Thursday night, four friends were deciding where to go on Saturday. Eun-ha suggested a hike, but Tomás said his knee still hurt, so he preferred something calmer. "How about a picnic by the river?" Priya proposed. Everyone liked the idea, but nobody wanted to be in charge of the food. After a short silence, Eun-ha said, "Why don't we each bring one thing? I'll make sandwiches, Priya can bring fruit, and Tomás could bring drinks." Tomás agreed at once, but Priya hesitated. "The fruit sounds good, but could I bring snacks instead? Fruit is so heavy to carry on the bus." They laughed and accepted the change. Before closing the chat, Eun-ha sent a final message: "Meet at the bus stop at nine. Don't forget your sunscreen!"

qs.q: Why did the group not choose Eun-ha's first suggestion?
o: Tomás wanted a calmer activity because of his knee.
Priya thought the weather on Saturday would be too hot for walking.
The river was closed to visitors on Saturday.
Nobody had a way to get to the mountain.
qs.why: Tomás의 무릎이 아파서 더 차분한 활동을 원했어요.

qs.q: How did the friends settle the problem of the food?
o: They decided to buy lunch at a restaurant.
Eun-ha volunteered to prepare everything alone.
They asked a classmate to cook for them.
Each of them agreed to bring one item.
qs.why: 각자 한 가지씩 가져오기로 했어요.

qs.q: Why did Priya ask to change her task?
o: She was allergic to the fruit.
She wanted to cook a hot meal instead.
She felt fruit would be difficult to carry.
She disliked making sandwiches.
qs.why: 버스에서 과일 들고 가기가 무겁다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of Eun-ha's last message?
o: To cancel the picnic because of bad weather in the afternoon
To confirm where and when to meet and to give a reminder
To invite another friend to the trip
To ask who was bringing the drinks
qs.why: 만나는 시간과 장소, 자외선 차단제 준비를 알려 주는 메시지예요.

qs.q: Which sentence is a suggestion about where to go on Saturday?
o: Could I bring snacks instead of fruit?
How about a picnic by the river?
I'll make sandwiches for everyone.
Tomás could bring drinks for the picnic.
qs.why: 'How about ...?'은 제안할 때 쓰는 표현이에요. Priya가 강가 소풍을 제안했어요.

items.title: Preparing for a Job Interview
items.text: Many young people feel anxious before their first job interview, but a little preparation can make a big difference. Start by learning about the company: read its website and think of one question you would like to ask the interviewer. Next, practice answering common questions aloud, such as "Why do you want this job?" Aim for answers that are clear and brief, with one real example from school or volunteer work. On the day, arrive ten minutes early and greet everyone with a firm handshake and eye contact. If you do not understand a question, it is perfectly fine to say, "Could you rephrase that, please?" Finally, close the interview by thanking the person for their time. A short thank-you message the same evening shows that you are considerate and truly interested in the position.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Interviewers always prefer applicants with a long work experience.
Handshakes are more important than answers.
Nervous people should avoid applying for jobs.
Careful preparation can help a person succeed in an interview.
qs.why: 면접 준비의 구체적인 방법들을 안내하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer suggest doing before the interview?
o: Memorizing a long speech about your whole life and school record
Asking friends to answer the questions for you
Learning about the company and thinking of a question to ask
Sending the interviewer a gift
qs.why: 회사를 조사하고 질문 하나를 생각해 두라고 해요.

qs.q: What should you do if you do not understand a question?
o: Answer something else and hope for the best
Politely ask the interviewer to say it in another way
Stay silent until the interviewer moves on
Ask the interviewer to skip the question
qs.why: Could you rephrase that, please?라고 물어도 괜찮다고 해요.

qs.q: Why does the writer recommend sending a thank-you message?
o: It shows consideration and interest in the position.
It guarantees that you will get the job within a few days.
It is required by law in most companies.
It helps you remember the interviewer's name.
qs.why: 배려심과 관심을 보여 준다고 마지막 문장에서 말해요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "firm" in "a firm handshake" is closest in meaning to
o: gentle and weak
quick and short
strong and steady
friendly and warm
qs.why: firm handshake는 힘 있고 안정된 악수를 뜻해서 strong and steady와 가장 가까워요.

items.title: Which Way to the Station?
items.text: A tourist with a large backpack stopped Arman on a busy street and asked, "Excuse me, do you know how to get to the train station?" Arman thought for a moment. "It's about ten minutes on foot. Go straight until you reach the traffic light, then turn right and walk past the post office. The station is across from a big bookstore, so you can't miss it." The tourist repeated the directions to check them, and Arman corrected one detail: the bookstore was on the left, not the right. Realizing that the man looked worried about his train, Arman added, "If you hurry, you'll make it. The trains to the airport leave every fifteen minutes." The tourist smiled with relief, thanked him warmly, and quickly disappeared into the crowd.

qs.q: What did the tourist ask Arman?
o: Where he could buy a backpack
Which bus went to the airport
How he could reach the train station
What time the post office closed
qs.why: 기차역에 가는 길을 물었어요.

qs.q: What is the first thing Arman tells the tourist to do?
o: Turn right at the post office near the bookstore
Go straight to the traffic light
Walk into the bookstore
Take a train to the airport
qs.why: 신호등까지 직진한 다음 오른쪽으로 돌라고 해요.

qs.q: Why did the tourist repeat the directions?
o: To check that he had understood them
To thank Arman for his kindness and say goodbye
To ask for a map of the city
To practice a new language
qs.why: 확인하려고 되풀이했고 Arman이 한 가지를 고쳐 줬어요.

qs.q: What did Arman correct?
o: The distance from the corner to the train station
The name of the street where the post office stood
The time of the next train to the airport
The side of the street on which the bookstore stood
qs.why: 서점은 오른쪽이 아니라 왼쪽에 있다고 고쳤어요.

qs.q: Why did Arman say, "If you hurry, you'll make it"?
o: He wanted the tourist to leave him alone because he was in a hurry himself.
He thought the station was about to close.
He noticed the man seemed worried about catching his train.
He was late for his own appointment.
qs.why: 남자가 기차를 놓칠까 걱정하는 것을 알아차렸기 때문이에요.

items.title: A Note for the Neighbor
items.text:
Dear Ms. Carter,

I'm Jaehyun from apartment 304, right above you. I wanted to apologize in person, but I missed you in the hallway twice, so I am leaving this note. On Saturday night I had some friends over to study, and I realize we were far louder than we should have been, especially after ten o'clock. I can only imagine how tiring that must have been after a long day. I assure you it will not happen again; from now on, we will move to the library after nine. If anything else ever disturbs you, please feel free to knock on my door or leave a message. I would much rather hear about a problem early than have it grow into something bigger. I have left a small box of tea at your door as a token of my regret.

Best wishes,
Jaehyun

qs.q: Why did Jaehyun write the note?
o: To invite Ms. Carter to a study party
To apologize for making too much noise
To complain about noise from her apartment
To ask her to look after his keys
qs.why: 토요일 밤 소음에 대해 사과하려고 쓴 쪽지예요.

qs.q: Why did he write instead of speaking to her?
o: He had not been able to meet her in the hallway.
He thought a written note was less polite.
He was too shy to knock on her door.
She had asked him to send her a message.
qs.why: 복도에서 두 번 마주치지 못했다고 해요.

qs.q: What does Jaehyun promise?
o: He will move to a different apartment before the end of the month.

items.title: The Power of Listening
items.text: Good communication is not only about speaking well; it also depends on how well we listen. Researchers on conversation often describe "active listening," which means giving full attention to the speaker instead of preparing your own reply. Active listeners show that they care in small ways: they look at the speaker, nod occasionally, and avoid checking their phones. They may also say "I see" or "That sounds difficult" to show that they follow the speaker's feelings. When necessary, they summarize what they heard, for example, "So you're worried about the exam on Monday?" This gives the speaker a chance to correct any misunderstanding. Surprisingly, people who feel truly heard are more likely to trust the listener and to calm down when they are upset.

qs.q: What does "active listening" mean in the passage?
o: Speaking continuously so that the other person stays quiet and listens to you
Paying full attention to the speaker rather than planning your answer
Taking written notes about everything a person says
Repeating every sentence in a louder voice

items.title: Returning a Sweater
items.text: Last weekend, Mina bought a blue sweater as a gift for her uncle, but when he opened the box, it was two sizes too small. On Monday she brought it back to the store with the receipt. At the counter she said, "Hello, I'd like to exchange this for a larger size, if possible." The clerk examined the tag and answered that the larger size was sold out, but she could either get a refund or choose a different color from the same line. Mina checked her phone and realized the store's website listed a gray one in the right size. After a short pause, she said, "I'd like the gray one, please." The clerk packed it carefully, wished her a nice week, and handed over the bag with a smile.

items.title: Opening a Bank Account
items.text: When Seoyeon turned seventeen, her parents suggested that she open her first bank account. At the bank she was greeted by an adviser named Mr. Lim, who asked her to sit down and explained the basics. "There are two kinds of accounts for teenagers," he said. "One pays a small amount of interest but lets you take your money out at any time. The other pays more, though you can't touch the money for a year." Seoyeon asked what documents she needed, and he listed her ID card and a form signed by a parent. She decided on the first type because she was saving for a laptop and might need the money sooner. Mr. Lim praised her sensible choice, and the whole process took only about twenty minutes.

items.title: Leaving a Good Phone Message
items.text: Many people dislike voicemail, yet a well-planned message can save time for everyone. Begin with your name and the reason you are calling, and speak clearly at a steady speed. If you leave a phone number, say it slowly, and repeat it at the end because listeners often need a second chance to write it down. Give one clear request, such as "Please call me back before noon," instead of a long explanation. It is also polite to say when you will be available, so the other person can plan. Finally, thank them and say goodbye briefly. Avoid spending the whole message apologizing or saying "um" again and again. A good message should last no more than thirty seconds, and if it takes longer, consider sending a text or an email instead.

qs.q: What is the main idea?
o: A short, clear voicemail makes communication easier.
Voicemail is always better than a text message.
People should never leave a phone number.
Phone calls are more polite than emails.

items.title: Disagreeing Without Arguing
items.text: In school projects, disagreement is almost unavoidable, but it does not have to lead to an argument. The key is to separate the idea from the person. Instead of saying, "That's a terrible plan," try, "I see what you mean, but I'm worried about the cost." Beginning with a point of agreement shows that you have listened. You can then use a softener such as "I'm not sure that..." or "Maybe we could..." to offer your alternative gently. It also helps to ask questions: "What do you think would happen if we changed the date?" This invites the other person to think with you rather than defend himself. If the discussion becomes heated, it is wise to take a short break. Often the best solution is a mixture of both ideas.

items.title: Dinner With a Host Family
items.text: On her first evening in Canada, Yuna sat at a large wooden table with her host family. The mother, Mrs. Collins, passed her a dish and said, "Please help yourself." Yuna was unsure what to say, so she simply said, "Thank you. It smells delicious." This made everyone smile. The father asked about her flight, and she described the long wait in the airport and the movie she watched. When the youngest child asked about her favorite food, Yuna laughed and said she liked spicy soup, and a lively conversation about different cuisines followed. At one point Yuna did not catch a word and said, "Sorry, could you say that again?" Mr. Collins repeated it slowly, and she realized she had worried too much. By the end of dinner, she felt much more at ease.

items.title: Volunteer Orientation
items.text: Welcome to the Green Park Cleanup Team! Before we begin, please listen to a few simple instructions. If you find something sharp, don't touch it; call a team leader, who will handle it with special tools. Third, sort the trash into the colored bags: blue for plastics, yellow for paper, and black for everything else. We will take a break at eleven, and snacks will be provided. items.title: Interview With a Young Baker
items.text:
Reporter: How did you become interested in baking?

items.title: Saying It Again in Another Way
items.text: At the school science fair, Hyunwoo was explaining his project on solar-powered chargers to a visitor from another school. The visitor, who was an exchange student, looked puzzled and said, "Sorry, what does 'panel' mean?" Hyunwoo had never thought about how to define it, but he did not panic. "It's a flat piece, usually rectangular, that catches sunlight," he said, drawing a shape in the air. Then he pointed at the device on the table. "This part. It turns light into electricity." The visitor's face brightened and she nodded. Later, Hyunwoo told his teacher that he had learned something important: when you cannot find an exact word, you can describe it, give an example, or use your hands, and the message will usually get through.

items.title: Small Talk at the Bus Stop
items.text: Small talk may seem unimportant, but it often builds the first bridge between strangers. On a rainy morning, a woman standing at the bus stop said to the man beside her, "This weather is awful, isn't it?" He replied, "It is. I forgot my umbrella, so I'm hoping the bus comes soon." She offered to share hers, and they began chatting about the traffic, the new bakery on the corner, and the best way to avoid crowds. They did not exchange names or phone numbers, but when the bus finally arrived, both felt a little brighter than before. Communication experts say that these brief, friendly exchanges can improve our mood and make a community feel safer. The secret is to choose a light subject, stay positive, and know when to stop.

items.title: Talking to the School Nurse
items.text: Dohyun walked into the school nurse's room holding his stomach. "I don't feel well," he said quietly. The nurse, Ms. Kang, invited him to sit and asked gentle questions. She took his temperature, which was normal, and suggested that he rest for twenty minutes on the bed and drink some warm water. She also told him that skipping breakfast can cause stomachaches, and she encouraged him to tell his teacher if it got worse. After resting, Dohyun felt better and thanked her before going back to class.

items.title: How to Respond to a Compliment
items.text: In many English-speaking countries, the usual reply to a compliment is a simple "Thank you." If someone says, "You gave a great presentation," answering "No, it was terrible" may make the speaker feel embarrassed, because it seems to reject their opinion. A better response is, "Thanks, I'm glad you enjoyed it." You may add a short comment, such as "I worked on it all weekend," to continue the conversation. Learners from cultures where modesty is valued sometimes feel it is boastful to accept praise so directly, but a warm thanks is generally considered both polite and humble. It is also friendly to return the compliment when it is sincere, for example, "Your slides looked great too." Remember that these are habits, not strict rules, and customs can differ among families and regions.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
o: To teach how to give a good presentation in English class
To explain a common way to respond to praise in English
To argue that modesty is a bad habit
To list the customs of one country
qs.why: 영어권에서 칭찬에 답하는 일반적인 방식을 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Why might the answer "No, it was terrible" cause trouble?
o: It may seem to reject the speaker's opinion.
It sounds too proud to the listener.
It is too short to be polite.
It usually starts an argument about homework.
qs.why: 상대의 의견을 거부하는 것처럼 보여 당황하게 할 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does the writer suggest adding after saying thanks?
o: A long explanation of your success
A question about the speaker's income
A request for another compliment
A short comment to keep the conversation going
qs.why: 대화를 이어 가기 위해 짧은 덧말을 더하라고 해요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last sentence?
o: To announce that customs are all the same in English-speaking countries
To correct a mistake in the first paragraph
To warn readers not to treat the advice as a fixed rule
To advertise a book about manners
qs.why: 습관일 뿐 엄격한 규칙이 아니라고 일반화에 주의를 줘요.

qs.q: The word "sincere" is closest in meaning to
o: quick and brief
honest and truly meant
loud and cheerful
formal and old-fashioned
qs.why: sincere는 진심에서 우러난 것을 뜻해요.

items.title: Handling a Difficult Question
items.text: After finishing her presentation on plastic waste, Jisoo opened the floor for questions. A boy in the back row asked, "Isn't it true that recycling doesn't really work?" The question was challenging, and for a second she felt her cheeks go warm. Instead of becoming defensive, she took a breath and replied, "That's a fair question. Recycling has real limits; some plastics cannot be reused. But it still reduces waste when combined with using less in the first place." She then asked the boy what he had read about the topic, which turned the exchange into a discussion. Her teacher later praised the way she stayed calm, admitted the limits of her argument, and kept the audience involved. "A good speaker doesn't have to know everything," he said. "She has to answer honestly."

qs.q: How did Jisoo feel when the boy asked his question?
o: A little embarrassed or pressured
Completely bored by the question
Proud and relaxed
Very angry at the boy
qs.why: 뺨이 따뜻해졌다는 표현은 약간 당황하거나 압박을 느꼈다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How did Jisoo respond?
o: She ignored the question and quickly changed the topic to something else.
She claimed that recycling solved everything.
She told the boy to read more before asking.
She accepted the limits of recycling and gave a balanced answer.
qs.why: 재활용의 한계를 인정하면서도 균형 잡힌 답을 했어요.

qs.q: Why did Jisoo ask the boy what he had read?
o: To prove that he was wrong
To check whether he had cheated
To involve him and continue the discussion
To end the question time quickly
qs.why: 그에게 질문을 돌려 토론으로 바꾸었어요.

qs.q: What does the teacher's last statement suggest?
o: Speakers should avoid answering questions.
Honesty matters more than knowing every answer.
Teachers must always correct students in public.
A presentation is only successful if no one disagrees.
qs.why: '모든 것을 알 필요는 없고 정직하게 대답하면 된다'는 뜻이에요.

items.title: A Group Meeting That Worked
items.text: The student council had only forty minutes to plan the school festival, and the previous meeting had ended in confusion. This time, the president, Haneul, began by stating the goal: "By four o'clock we should decide who does what." She asked each member to speak for one minute, and she wrote the main ideas on the board. When two members started talking at the same time, she said, "Let's hear Minho first, then Eva." Whenever someone made a suggestion, she repeated it in her own words to be sure she understood. By ten to four, the tasks had been divided, and a deadline was set beside each name. As the members packed their bags, one of them said it was the first meeting that had felt useful. Haneul smiled. "It's simple," she said. "Everyone talks, everyone listens."

qs.q: What was different about this meeting?
o: The leader organized the discussion with clear steps.
The meeting lasted longer than any earlier one that term.
More members attended than before.
It was held outside the school.
qs.why: 회장이 목표를 밝히고 발언 시간을 나누는 등 체계적으로 진행했어요.

qs.q: What did Haneul do when two members spoke at once?
o: She asked both of them to leave the room until they agreed.
She ended the meeting immediately.
She let them finish together.
She decided the order in which they would speak.
qs.why: 먼저 Minho, 그다음 Eva라고 순서를 정했어요.

qs.q: Why did Haneul repeat suggestions in her own words?
o: To make the suggestions sound better
To give the members time to rest
To check that she had understood them
To show she disagreed with them
qs.why: 이해했는지 확인하기 위해서예요.

qs.q: What does Haneul's final remark mean?
o: Only the leader should speak in meetings to save time.
A meeting works when everyone shares and listens.
Every meeting should be forty minutes long.
Tasks are best given without a deadline.
qs.why: 모두가 말하고 모두가 듣는 것이 성공 비결이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which detail is stated in the passage?
o: The goal was to finish the plan by four o'clock.
The festival will take place in the spring.
The meeting began at three o'clock sharp.
Each member spoke for five minutes.
qs.why: 4시까지 역할을 정하는 것이 목표라고 명시돼요.

items.title: Booking a Table by Phone
items.text:
Host: Good evening, Olive Tree Kitchen. How may I help you?
Customer: Hi, I'd like to reserve a table for six on Saturday evening, if you have one.
Host: Let me check. What time were you thinking?
Customer: Around seven would be ideal. It's for my father's retirement dinner.
Host: Congratulations to him! Unfortunately, seven is fully booked, but I can offer a table at six thirty or one at eight fifteen.
Customer: Hmm, my grandmother goes to bed early, so six thirty would be better. Is there a quiet corner?
Host: Yes, there's a round table near the window, away from the kitchen. May I have your name and number?
Customer: It's Kim, and my number is 555-0142.
Host: Thank you, Ms. Kim. One more thing: if you'd like a cake, you're welcome to bring one, and we will not charge a serving fee.
Customer: That's very thoughtful. Thank you so much.

qs.q: Why is the customer making the reservation?
o: To hold a birthday party for her grandmother
To meet a friend after work
To thank the restaurant staff
To celebrate her father's retirement
qs.why: 아버지의 은퇴 기념 저녁 식사 때문이에요.

qs.q: Why does the customer choose six thirty?
o: She prefers to eat before the restaurant gets crowded.
The later table was too far from the kitchen.
Her grandmother goes to bed early.
The host said that seven was cheaper.
qs.why: 할머니가 일찍 주무시기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does the host say about a cake?
o: The restaurant will bake one for free if you order early.
The family may bring one without an extra charge.
Cakes are not permitted inside the restaurant.
A serving fee must be paid in advance.
qs.why: 케이크를 가져와도 서빙 요금이 없다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the host's purpose in saying "Congratulations to him!"?
o: To respond kindly to the personal news
To change the reservation date
To ask for the father's name and age
To end the call politely
qs.why: 고객이 알려 준 개인적인 소식에 친절히 반응한 거예요.

qs.q: Where is the table the host offers?
o: Next to the kitchen door at the back
In the center of the large dining room
Outside on the patio under the trees
Near the window and away from the kitchen
qs.why: 창가의 둥근 테이블이고 주방과 떨어져 있다고 해요.

items.title: Can I Borrow Your Notes?
items.text:
Jina: Hey, Marcus, do you have a minute?
Marcus: Sure. What's up?
Jina: I was in the clinic yesterday and missed the history lecture. Would you mind lending me your notes?
Marcus: Of course, but my handwriting is awful. You might have trouble reading it.
Jina: That's fine. I'd just like to see the main points before the quiz on Friday.
Marcus: Then why don't I scan the pages and send them tonight? That way I can keep the originals in case I need them.
Jina: That would be perfect. Thank you! I'll buy you a drink next time.
Marcus: No need. Actually, the teacher mentioned that the quiz will focus on the last two chapters, so concentrate on those.
Jina: Really? You're a lifesaver. I'd have wasted hours on the early part.
Marcus: Anytime. Let me know if anything is hard to understand.

qs.q: Why does Jina need Marcus's notes?
o: She lost her own notebook on the way to school and needs another.
She wants to compare answers on the quiz.
She missed a lecture because she was at the clinic.
She forgot which chapter was assigned.
qs.why: 어제 진료소에 가서 수업을 놓쳤어요.

qs.q: What does Marcus offer to do?
o: Give her his notebook for a week
Scan the pages and send them that night
Explain the lecture to her in person
Write a new summary for the class
qs.why: 스캔해서 오늘 밤 보내 주겠다고 해요.

qs.q: What useful information does Marcus add?
o: The quiz will mostly cover the last two chapters.
The quiz has been moved to a later week by the teacher.
The teacher will let students use notes.
The lecture was recorded for absent students.
qs.why: 퀴즈가 마지막 두 단원에 집중될 거라고 알려 줘요.

qs.q: What does "You're a lifesaver" express?
o: A joke about a medical emergency at the clinic
Disappointment about a missed class
A refusal of the offer
Strong gratitude for very helpful advice
qs.why: 'You're a lifesaver'는 큰 도움을 준 데 대한 고마움을 나타내요.

qs.q: Why does Marcus say "my handwriting is awful"?
o: He is politely refusing to lend his notes to her this week.
He wants her to practice her own writing before the quiz.
He is warning her that his notes might be hard to read.
He is asking her to rewrite the notes in neater handwriting.
qs.why: 글씨가 엉망이라 읽기 어려울 수 있다는 주의를 주는 말이에요.

items.title: At the Store Counter
items.text:
Customer: Excuse me, I bought this jacket here last week, but the zipper broke the first time I used it.
Clerk: I'm so sorry to hear that. May I see your receipt?
Customer: Here it is. I'd like to exchange it for another one, if that's possible.
Clerk: Let me check. Yes, you're still within the thirty-day return period. Would you like the same style, or would you prefer a refund?
Customer: I really like this style, so I'd rather have the same jacket in my size.
Clerk: Unfortunately, we only have it in black now. The navy one is sold out.
Customer: Black is fine, as long as the zipper works.
Clerk: I tested the zipper myself, and it works smoothly. I'll also include a card for an extra year of repairs.
Customer: That's very helpful. Thank you for sorting this out so quickly.
Clerk: My pleasure. Enjoy your new jacket.

qs.q: What is the customer's problem?
o: The jacket was the wrong size for the customer.
The zipper on a new jacket broke.
The store charged her too much.
The color faded after one wash.
qs.why: 새 재킷의 지퍼가 처음 사용할 때 고장 났어요.

qs.q: Why does the customer accept a black jacket?
o: She likes the style and the zipper works.
The navy one costs more than the black one.
She dislikes the color navy and prefers black.
The clerk insisted that she take the black one.
qs.why: 스타일이 마음에 들고 지퍼가 잘 작동하면 괜찮다고 해요.

qs.q: What extra service does the clerk give?
o: A discount on a future purchase at the store
Free delivery of the jacket
A refund of the original price
A card for another year of repairs
qs.why: 수선 1년 추가 카드를 준다고 해요.

qs.q: What does the clerk's last remark "My pleasure" show?
o: An apology for the customer's trouble
A warning about the store's policy
A polite reply to the customer's thanks
A request for the customer to return later
qs.why: 'My pleasure'는 감사 인사에 대한 공손한 응답이에요.

items.title: At the Lost Property Office
items.text:
Staff: Good afternoon. How can I help you?
Passenger: Hello. I think I left my laptop bag on the train this morning. I got off at the last stop, and when I got to work, it was gone.
Staff: I'm sorry about that. Can you describe the bag?
Passenger: It's a dark gray backpack with a red tag on the zipper. There's also a small sticker of a mountain on the front.
Staff: And roughly what time was the train?
Passenger: It left Central Station at about eight fifteen, and I sat in the third carriage.
Staff: Hold on a moment while I check the list. Yes, a gray backpack was handed in by a cleaner an hour ago. Can you tell me what's inside?
Passenger: A laptop, a blue notebook, and a charger with a yellow cable.
Staff: That matches. Please show me your ID, and you can take it.
Passenger: Thank you so much. I was so worried!

qs.q: What did the passenger lose?
o: A blue notebook on the platform
A gray backpack with a laptop
A phone with a yellow cable
A coat with a red tag
qs.why: 노트북이 든 회색 배낭을 잃어버렸어요.

qs.q: Why does the staff member ask what is inside the bag?
o: To confirm that it belongs to the passenger
To find out how heavy it is before carrying it
To decide how much to charge
To see whether it is dangerous
qs.why: 소지품을 말하게 해 주인임을 확인하려는 거예요.

qs.q: Who found the bag?
o: Another passenger on the platform
The station's security camera
The passenger's colleague
A cleaner who handed it in
qs.why: 청소원이 한 시간 전에 맡겼다고 해요.

qs.q: What must the passenger show before taking the bag?
o: A train ticket
A receipt for the laptop
An ID
A letter from his employer
qs.why: 신분증을 보여 달라고 해요.

qs.q: What does "Hold on a moment" ask the passenger to do?
o: Speak more slowly
Wait briefly
Come back tomorrow
Describe the bag again
qs.why: 'Hold on a moment'는 잠시 기다려 달라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Your friend says, "I'm sorry, but I can't make it to your party on Saturday." Which reply is the most appropriate?
o: Never mind. I wasn't going to invite you in the first place.
That's too bad. Maybe we can get together some other time.
Great, because I really wanted fewer people to come.
You can't? Then I'll cancel the whole party for you.
items.why: 거절을 받아들이고 다음을 기약하는 응답이 적절해요.

items.q: A caller says, "Hello, may I speak to Ms. Park, please?" Which reply is the most natural for the receptionist?
o: I'm afraid she's in a meeting right now. Can I take a message?
Yes, I am speaking to Ms. Park, and she is very well.
She spoke to me yesterday, so I know her quite well.
Please send a letter because phones are not for talking.
items.why: 전화 응대에서는 부재를 알리고 메시지를 받겠다고 하는 것이 자연스러워요.

items.q: A guest says to the host, "It's a little cold in here, isn't it?" What does the guest most likely want?
o: The host to explain how the weather forecast works
The host to give her the price of the room
The host to tell her where the thermometer is
The host to close the window or turn up the heat
items.why: 간접적인 표현으로 창문을 닫거나 난방을 올려 달라는 완곡한 요청이에요.

items.q: Which request is the most polite way to ask a teacher to explain something again?
o: Hey, could you just say all that stuff one more time for me?
Say that again, I wasn't paying attention at all.
Excuse me, would you mind explaining that once more?
What? I didn't get any of it, so go back.
items.why: would you mind -ing는 정중한 요청 표현이에요.

items.q: Your friend says, "We've been working for six hours. Let's call it a day." What does your friend mean?
o: Let's start the project again tomorrow morning at six.
Let's stop working for now.
Let's phone each other every day this week.
Let's decide on a date for the party.
items.why: call it a day는 '오늘 일은 여기까지 하자'는 관용 표현이에요.

items.q: When someone says, "I'll take a rain check," what do they usually mean?
o: They cannot accept now but would like to do it another time.
They are ready to accept the invitation immediately.
They want to know about tomorrow's weather forecast.
They plan to pay the bill by personal check.
items.why: rain check는 지금은 거절하지만 다음에 하자는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Your friend asks, "Where should we eat tonight, pizza or noodles?" You answer, "It's up to you." What do you mean?
o: I do not want to eat anything tonight, so choose nothing.
I would like to pick the restaurant myself.
Please ask someone else to decide.
You can decide; either choice is fine with me.
items.why: It's up to you는 '네가 정해'라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Your friend's essay has a weak ending. Which comment is the most tactful?
o: Your ending is terrible, so you should write it again.
Nobody will understand your ending, so please don't hand it in tomorrow.
Your ideas are strong; maybe the ending could be a bit clearer.
The essay is fine, but I have not read the ending.
items.why: 장점을 먼저 말하고 완곡하게 개선점을 제안하는 것이 가장 배려 있는 표현이에요.

items.q: You want to add a point while a classmate is speaking. Which expression is the most appropriate?
o: Stop talking now, because I have something to say.
Sorry to interrupt, but may I add one point?
Be quiet for a second; my point is far better.
Excuse me, I will not add anything to your point.
items.why: Sorry to interrupt, but ...는 끼어들 때 쓰는 공손한 표현이에요.

items.q: You are talking with a new neighbor and want to end the conversation politely. What should you say?
o: It was great talking to you. I'd better get going.
You talk a lot, so I will leave now.
The conversation is over, and you may go.
I hope we never have to speak about this again.
items.why: 대화를 마무리할 때는 즐거웠다는 말과 함께 가봐야 한다고 말해요.

items.q: Your friend says, "I failed my driving test again." Which response shows the most sympathy?
o: Congratulations! You must be very pleased with yourself.
That's nice. What are we having for lunch today?
Well, you should have practiced a lot harder before the test, obviously.
Oh no, I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about it?
items.why: 공감과 위로를 담은 표현이 적절해요.

items.q: A speaker says, "So, if I understand you correctly, the meeting has moved to Friday?" What is she mainly doing?
o: Refusing to attend the meeting
Changing the topic of the conversation
Checking that she has understood the information
Offering to organize the next event
items.why: 'if I understand you correctly'는 이해한 바를 확인하는 표현이에요.

items.q: A student says, "I might be wrong, but I think the second plan costs more." Why does he begin with "I might be wrong"?
o: To show that he is completely certain about the facts
To make his opinion sound less forceful
To ask the listener for money
To end the discussion immediately
items.why: I might be wrong은 의견을 부드럽게 만드는 완화 표현(hedge)이에요.

items.q: Someone asks, "Could you give me a hand with these boxes?" What does the speaker want?
o: Your help in moving the boxes
You to applaud for the boxes
You to hold the boxes upside down
You to count the boxes for an hour
items.why: give me a hand는 '도와주다'라는 관용 표현이에요.

items.q: A friend says, "Thanks a lot for helping me move!" Which reply is the most natural?
o: Yes, I helped you a lot, so now you owe me.
It does not matter because I am not helped.
A lot of help is a lot of thanks for you.
No problem. I was glad to help.
items.why: 감사에는 No problem, You're welcome 등으로 응답해요.

items.q: A passer-by says, "The post office is right across from the bank." Where is the post office?
o: Inside the bank building on the second floor
Two streets away from the bank
On the opposite side of the street from the bank
Directly behind the bank building
items.why: across from은 '건너편에'라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: A customer says, "I asked for a small coffee, but this is a large." Which reply from the server is the most appropriate?
o: That's your problem, because you ordered it and I wrote it down.
I'm so sorry about that. I'll make you a small one right away.
Large is better, so just drink it anyway.
Small and large are the same thing here.
items.why: 실수를 인정하고 바로잡겠다고 하는 것이 적절한 서비스 응대예요.

items.q: Which opening is the most suitable for an email to a professor you have not met?
o: Dear Professor Kim, I am writing to ask about the assignment deadline.
Hey Prof, what's up with the assignment deadline this week?
Yo Professor Kim! Tell me the deadline fast.
Hi there, deadline question: when is it?
items.why: 교수님께는 격식 있는 호칭과 목적을 밝히는 문장이 적절해요.

items.q: A classmate says, "That's a lovely jacket!" Which reply is the most natural?
o: You are wrong, because you cannot see well.
I did not ask your opinion about my jacket.
Please stop looking at my clothes.
Thank you! I got it last week.
items.why: 칭찬에는 감사로 응답하는 것이 자연스러워요.

items.q: You want to suggest visiting the science museum on Saturday. Which sentence is correct?
o: How about go to the science museum on Saturday?
Why we don't go to the science museum on Saturday?
How about going to the science museum on Saturday?
Let's to go to the science museum on Saturday.
items.why: How about + -ing 형태로 제안해요.

items.q: You see a stranger struggling with a heavy bag. Which sentence offers help in a natural way?
o: Do you want that I carry your bag to the station?
Would you like me to carry that bag for you?
Will you carrying my bag, please?
May I to carry your bag for you?
items.why: Would you like me to + 동사원형은 도움을 제안하는 자연스러운 표현이에요.

items.q: At a first meeting, which question is NOT appropriate for small talk?

What do you like to do on weekends?
How was your trip here?
Have you been to this café before?
items.why: 소득은 처음 만난 사이에 묻기에 부적절한 사적인 질문이에요.

items.q: Your teammate says, "We should use the blue poster." You see it differently. Which reply disagrees politely?
o: That is nonsense, and you know it.
I couldn't agree more with you.
You are completely wrong about everything, as usual, and I know it.
That's a fair point, but I see it a little differently.
items.why: 상대 의견을 인정하며 부드럽게 반대하는 표현이에요.

items.q: A friend says, "I'm terribly sorry for being late. The bus broke down." Which reply accepts the apology?
o: I will never forgive you for this.
You should have taken a taxi, obviously.

No excuses are allowed in my meetings.
items.why: That's all right는 사과를 받아들이는 표현이에요.

items.q: A receptionist says on the phone, "Please hold the line." What should the caller do?

Wait on the phone without hanging up
Speak more loudly so she can hear
Give her a different phone number

items.q: Which sentence is the most indirect and polite way to ask to borrow a classmate's notes?
o: I was wondering if you could lend me your notes.
Lend me your notes.
Give me your notes right now, please, I need them.
I want your notes, so lend them.
items.why: I was wondering if ...는 매우 완곡한 요청 표현이에요.

items.q: Someone asks, "Would you like tea or coffee?" You prefer tea. Which reply is correct?
o: I'd rather to have tea, please.
I'd rather having tea, please.
I'd rather had tea, please.
I'd rather have tea, please.
items.why: would rather 다음에는 동사원형이 와요.

items.q: Which closing is the most suitable for a formal letter that begins "Dear Mr. Smith"?
o: Cheers, see you soon, Minji
See ya later, Minji
Sincerely, Minji Han
Your pal, Minji
items.why: 격식 있는 편지는 Sincerely로 끝맺는 것이 알맞아요.

items.q: Someone says, "I said Tuesday, not Thursday. We need to meet on Tuesday." What is the speaker doing?
o: Apologizing for arriving late
Correcting a misunderstanding about the day
Refusing an invitation to a meeting
Asking for directions to the office
items.why: 잘못 이해한 요일을 바로잡고 있어요.

items.good: Could you tell me where the post office is?
bad: Could you tell me where is the post office?
Could you tell me where the post office?
Could you tell me where does the post office is?

cz.st: Could you tell me where the post office ___?

items.rule: 간접 의문문에서는 의문사 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 순서를 써요.

items.good: Would you mind opening the window?
bad: Would you mind to open the window?
Would you mind open the window?
Would you mind opened the window?
items.rule: Would you mind 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와요.
items.hint: mind 뒤에 오는 동사의 형태를 생각해 보세요.

items.good: I wish you had told me earlier.
items.ko: 네가 더 일찍 말해 주었더라면 좋았을 텐데.
bad: I wish you have told me earlier.
I wish you had tell me earlier.
I wish you telling me earlier.
items.rule: 과거 사실에 대한 아쉬움은 wish + 과거완료(had p.p.)로 나타내요.
items.hint: 과거에 일어나지 않은 일에 대한 아쉬움이에요.

items.good: Do you happen to know what time the library closes?
items.ko: 도서관이 몇 시에 닫는지 혹시 아세요?
bad: Do you happen to know what time does the library close?
Do you happen knowing what time the library closes?
Do you happen to know what time the library close?

cz.st: Do you happen to know what time the library ___?

items.rule: 간접 의문문에서는 do/does를 쓰지 않고 '주어 + 동사' 순서이며, 주어가 3인칭 단수이므로 closes를 써요.

items.good: Not only did she apologize, but she also offered to pay for the damage.
items.ko: 그녀는 사과했을 뿐만 아니라 피해를 보상하겠다고도 제안했다.
bad: Not only she apologized, but she also offered to pay for the damage.
Not only did she apologized, but she also offered to pay for the damage.
Not only she did apologize, but she also offered to pay for the damage.

cz.st: Not only ___ she apologize, but she also offered to pay for the damage.

items.rule: Not only가 문장 앞에 오면 주어와 조동사가 도치되고, 본동사는 원형이 와요.

items.good: Let's meet at six, shall we?
bad: Let's meet at six, will we?
Let's meet at six, don't we?
Let's meet at six, are we?
items.rule: Let's로 시작하는 문장의 부가의문문은 shall we?를 써요.

items.good: I'm looking forward to hearing from you.
bad: I'm looking forward to hear from you.
I'm looking forward hearing from you.
I'm looking forward to heard from you.

cz.st: I'm looking forward to ___ from you.

items.rule: look forward to에서 to는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사가 와요.
items.hint: to 뒤에 오는 말의 형태를 생각해 보세요.

items.good: She suggested that we take a different route.
items.ko: 그녀는 우리에게 다른 길로 가자고 제안했다.
bad: She suggested us to take a different route.
She suggested that we to take a different route.
She suggested to take us a different route.

cz.st: She suggested that we ___ a different route.

items.rule: suggest 뒤의 that절에는 '주어 + 동사원형' 형태를 쓰고, suggest는 'suggest + 목적어 + to부정사'로 쓸 수 없어요.
